state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 259 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 277 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

arm_A.rule: max(records, key=objective) -- the public route's default

arm_B.rule: argmax R over candidates passing quality, survival and local evidence

representative.centroid_rule: a centroid that has not been evaluated is a proposal, not a selection; it must be run before it can be deployed (guide 7.3)
representative.medoid_rule: the medoid minimises the summed schema distance to the other ELIGIBLE candidates and does not replace R or the local probes

local_coverage.note: coverage is reported before any selection claim (guide L04.6)

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 294 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 224 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

arm_A.rule: max(records, key=objective) -- the public route's default

arm_B.rule: argmax R over candidates passing quality, survival and local evidence

representative.centroid_rule: a centroid that has not been evaluated is a proposal, not a selection; it must be run before it can be deployed (guide 7.3)
representative.medoid_rule: the medoid minimises the summed schema distance to the other ELIGIBLE candidates and does not replace R or the local probes

local_coverage.note: coverage is reported before any selection claim (guide L04.6)

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 311 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 259 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

arm_A.rule: max(records, key=objective) -- the public route's default

arm_B.rule: argmax R over candidates passing quality, survival and local evidence

representative.centroid_rule: a centroid that has not been evaluated is a proposal, not a selection; it must be run before it can be deployed (guide 7.3)
representative.medoid_rule: the medoid minimises the summed schema distance to the other ELIGIBLE candidates and does not replace R or the local probes

local_coverage.note: coverage is reported before any selection claim (guide L04.6)

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 277 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

arm_B.rule: argmax R over candidates passing quality, survival and local evidence

representative.centroid_rule: a centroid that has not been evaluated is a proposal, not a selection; it must be run before it can be deployed (guide 7.3)
representative.medoid_rule: the medoid minimises the summed schema distance to the other ELIGIBLE candidates and does not replace R or the local probes

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 294 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar
B.retention_note: the selector returned nothing admissible at any cutoff, so the incumbent seed was held for the whole window. That is the retention rule doing its job, and it is a reportable result rather than a failed cell

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 224 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar
B.retention_note: the selector returned nothing admissible at any cutoff, so the incumbent seed was held for the whole window. That is the retention rule doing its job, and it is a reportable result rather than a failed cell

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 311 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 259 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar
B.retention_note: the selector returned nothing admissible at any cutoff, so the incumbent seed was held for the whole window. That is the retention rule doing its job, and it is a reportable result rather than a failed cell

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 277 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 294 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar
B.retention_note: the selector returned nothing admissible at any cutoff, so the incumbent seed was held for the whole window. That is the retention rule doing its job, and it is a reportable result rather than a failed cell

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 224 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

A.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar

B.description: neighborhood selector on the same calendar

E.description: neighborhood selector plus bank and response policy
E.policy_note: LAB-06 measured ZERO switches for this policy on the registered thresholds, so E deploys D's schedule and its own contribution is null by construction here. That is reported, not hidden: E is an extension and never a substitute for C or D

B-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

C-A.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-B.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

D-C.pairing: same dates only; days where either arm was not live are excluded

(D-C)-(B-A).reading: the interaction: does regime timing add MORE to the new selector than to the old

state_tape_coverage.rule: the state tape must span the arm's whole window. A tape covering only part of it puts every dynamic refresh in that part, which is a coverage artefact and not a timing result

regime_schedule.source: 311 emitted state changes; the first inside each of 6 equal periods, with a 30-day minimum gap
regime_schedule.matched_rule: the dynamic arms get exactly as many refreshes as the calendar arms. The model chooses WHERE they fall, never how many, because a method allowed to look more times is not being compared on timing (guide 10.5)

compute_match.rule: same refresh count and same training memory. Only the timing differs, which is the contribution being measured (guide 10.1 arm C: 'training memory giữ như A')

controls.RISK_ONLY: the benefit is exposure timing, not parameter selection
controls.CALENDAR_MATCHED: the benefit is extra search compute, not better timing
controls.BANK_CALENDAR: the benefit is having a bank at all, not switching within it on regime
controls.STATE_PLACEBO: the benefit is switching on ANY persistent signal, not on this one
controls.DELAYED_STATE: the benefit disappears under a realistic observation delay
controls.EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC: how much of the ceiling is reachable only with hindsight
controls.USER_PRESET_REFERENCE: the supplied presets already do as well, retrospectively

registry.retention_rule: no control is dropped because it beats the proposed method (guide 10.2)
registry.staging_rule: controls are added in stages rather than as a full Cartesian product of every combination (guide 10.2)

RISK_ONLY.description: installed WFO selector on the frozen calendar
RISK_ONLY.note: arm A's own selections, resized by a scale calibrated on TRAINING observations of each state and clipped to [0.5, 1.0]. If this reproduces a dynamic arm's advantage, the advantage was exposure and not parameter selection

fidelity.why_it_matters: a placebo that switches far more often loses on transaction costs alone, and beating it would say nothing about the states. The control is only a control while the rates match (guide 10.2)

STATE_PLACEBO.generated_from: development-window dwell statistics only; no future label is shuffled in

CALENDAR_MATCHED.reason: the dynamic arms were given exactly the calendar's refresh count and training memory, so the calendar is already compute-matched to them. There is no separate run because there is no compute difference to control for

BANK_CALENDAR.reason: LAB-06 measured zero switches on the registered thresholds, so a bank that switches on the calendar and a bank that switches on regime deploy the same sequence. The control is retained and reported as degenerate rather than dropped (guide 10.2)

EXPOST_DIAGNOSTIC.reason: computed from returns that had not happened at decision time

checkpoint_note: each cell is written as it completes and reused on a later attempt, so a crash costs one cell rather than the whole run
